questions.q: The welcome note begins with a saying about joys. What is it?
options: Joys are few and sorrows many
This is not the saying used.
Joys shared are joys multiplied
So it is, says the note, with the joys of learning and intellectual pursuit.
Joy comes only after hardship
This is not the saying used.
Joys of the world never last
The note does contrast material joys, but this is not the saying.
questions.rationale: Through this magazine, Maulana Wahiduddin Khan’s discoveries about God’s creation plan, life, peace and practical wisdom are shared with the world.

questions.q: In his lecture at a church in Philadelphia, what did Maulana say peace is, according to Islam?
options: The summum bonum, the greatest good
This was the gist of his lecture on ‘Islam and Peace’.
A temporary arrangement
The lecture gave peace the highest place.
Useful only between nations
The article speaks of peace in individual and social life.
Less important than victory
The article says the opposite.
questions.rationale: Spirituality and peace are two sides of one coin. The essence of prayer is to live with a positive mind in a negative situation.

questions.q: What do scientists call the explosion in the great cosmic ball?
options: The ‘Great Flood’
This is not the term used.
The ‘First Dawn’
This is not the term used.
The ‘Long Night’
This is not the term used.
The ‘Big Bang’
After it, the particles scattered through space and later assembled in different forms.
questions.rationale: The Creator produced the universe by a long, complex process so that man might develop his thinking and reach God-realisation.

questions.q: At the exhibition in Delhi, what drew the crowds to the American pavilion?
options: A talking robot
This is not what the article describes.
A giant telescope
This is not what the article describes.
A flying car
It drove on the ground, hovered about four feet up, circled the field and landed.
A model of the moon
This is not what the article describes.
questions.rationale: Material wonders attract crowds, but a spiritual person holds inner peace dearer than anything and finds satisfaction in his own inner resources.

questions.q: According to the article, from whom should a believer ask for his rights?
options: From the government
The article regrets the strife caused by such demands.
Only from God
His own duty is to give others what is due from him.
From his employer
The article points away from agitation.
From his neighbours
This is not the teaching given.
questions.rationale: Islam wants us to build a duty-conscious society rather than a rights-conscious one. We do our duty faithfully, seeking God’s pleasure.

questions.q: Over what period were the chapters of the Quran revealed?
options: 23 years
They were sent bit by bit, according to circumstances.
3 years
The period was much longer.
40 years
This is not the figure given.
A single night
The article says they were not all revealed at one time.
questions.rationale: The Quran was both memorized and preserved in writing, so any copy anywhere is exactly the same as that handed down by the Prophet.

questions.q: Whom did the American scientists study to find out why one champion wins and another loses?
options: Chess grandmasters
This is not the group studied.
Long-distance runners
This is not the group studied.
Mountain climbers
This is not the group studied.
Top-ranked international wrestlers
They compared physical strength and psychological reserves.
questions.rationale: The difference lay in the mind: conviction that one’s goals are worthwhile, discipline, and cool thinking even in times of crisis.

questions.q: The article concludes that the only real option before us is between…
options: A ‘universe with God’ or a ‘universe without God’
The article says this is not the choice we actually have.
Science or religion
The article brings the two together.
A ‘universe with God’ or ‘no universe at all’
A universe without God is not one of the options.
Faith or reason
The article argues by reason.
questions.rationale: Intelligent creation is clearly proof of an Intelligent Creator; order cannot exist without an organiser.

questions.q: On which of these did the Prophet tell people to follow his own example?
options: Politics
The article notes that he never gave such advice about politics.
Prayer and Hajj
‘Perform your prayer as you see me performing it’; ‘Learn the method of Hajj from my practice.’
Trade
This is not mentioned.
Architecture
This is not mentioned.
questions.rationale: The political system in Islam rests on the social condition of the time; the article describes it as a people’s government rather than a theocratic one.

questions.q: What, according to the survey, is the secret of Japanese shipbuilders’ speed?
options: Teamwork
Workers and management function together in complete unison.
Cheaper steel
This is not the reason found.
Longer working hours
This is not the reason found.
Bigger shipyards
This is not the reason found.
questions.rationale: They build in eight months what takes others sixteen or twenty-four. Unity is the true key to organisational success.
